title: The People Who Cannot Stop Working

collection.credit:
ISOLA — BEYOND THE HORIZON: THE WORLD WE IMAGINE
A NEW, SEPARATE COMPANION EVENT ANTHOLOGY FOR VIRTUAL VILLAGERS 1–5
Version 1.0 | 40 original branching events
collection.description: A tired weaver asks whether distant societies give workers time to rest, or demand more labor than a person can bear.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A tired weaver asks whether distant societies give workers time to rest, or demand more labor than a person can bear.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The villagers design a hypothetical schedule with shared duties and predictable days off.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: A caregiver notes that unpaid responsibilities do not disappear when paid work ends.

text_only.reason: the word's everyday sense (a thing or a duty disappears); nobody goes missing

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: A laborer describes exhaustion, injury, and little time for family; the council examines its own workload.

text_only.reason: an injury imagined or discussed; nobody is hurt

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: A trader wonders whether some workers might accept long hours to support people they love.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The group agrees that food and shelter matter, but so do purpose, dignity, and leisure.

text_only.reason: food talked about or imagined; the village's stores do not change

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: A villager says meaningful work can still be tiring; the group resists easy slogans.
